## About

Figures from the knitr graphics devices used in practice, webp, svg, and pdf,
for a wide collage and a standard plot. Every figure has the `#| panzoom: true`
cell option and opens in panzoom unless its case says otherwise. Figure shapes
and how they open are on [wide and tall figures](h-wide.html).

knitr has no built-in webp device, so these use `agg_webp` from ragg, which
needs `units = "in"` because knitr passes sizes in inches.

The cases below draw with this helper (`ragg` writes the webp files):

```{r}
library(ragg)

# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(
      cumsum(rnorm(200)),
      type = "l",
      main = paste("Panel", i),
      xlab = "",
      ylab = "",
      col = hcl.colors(n)[i],
      lwd = 2
    )
  }
}
```

## 1. webp collage {#c1 expect-fit="height"}

A 25 × 2 inch collage written as webp. It opens in panzoom at screen height.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (webp)."

collage(n = 12)
```

## 2. svg collage {#c2 expect-fit="height"}

The same collage written as svg. It opens in panzoom at screen height.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: svg
#| fig-cap: "The collage as svg."

collage(n = 12)
```

## 3. webp plot {#c3 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none" expect-scale="1"}

A small plot written as webp. It opens in panzoom at its real size.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "A standard-size plot as webp."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 4. svg plot {#c4 expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

The same plot written as svg. It opens in panzoom at its real size.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: svg
#| fig-cap: "A standard-size plot as svg."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 5. png and pdf {#c5 expect-fit="contain"}

A plot written as both png and pdf. The page shows the png, which opens in
panzoom.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, pdf written alongside."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 6. png and cairo_pdf {#c6 expect-fit="contain"}

Case 5 with the cairo PDF device, which embeds fonts and handles Unicode (µ,
Greek letters) and transparency better than `pdf`. The page shows the png, which
opens in panzoom. With a PDF device alone, there is no image to open. Quarto
embeds the PDF in a small box with the browser's PDF viewer, which panzoom
leaves alone.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "cairo_pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (mu = 5, alpha = 0.05)."

filled.contour(
  volcano,
  color.palette = terrain.colors,
  plot.title = title(main = "mu = 5, alpha = 0.05")
)
```

## 7. webp past its size limit {#c7}

A 100 × 5 inch collage as webp at 192 dpi. At 19,200 px wide it is past the webp
limit of 16,383 px per side, so ragg can't write the file. The page shows a
broken image, and clicking it opens an empty viewer.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 192)
#| fig-cap: "The collage as webp at 192 dpi."
#| error: true

collage(n = 12)
```
